nodes.name: Hydrothermal SnS₂ synthesis
nodes.procedure: SnS₂ NSs were synthesized by a hydrothermal treatment with SnCl₄·5H₂O and thiourea at 190°C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: SnS₂ NSs were synthesized by a hydrothermal treatment with SnCl₄·5H₂O and thiourea at 190°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Partial oxidation to SnS₂/SnO₂ heterostructures
nodes.procedure: SnS₂/SnO₂ heterostructures were obtained through the partial oxidation of SnS₂ NSs by diluted H₂O₂ at 140°C. By manipulating the oxidation time (x = 60, 90, and 120 min) of SnS₂ (denoted as SnS₂/SnO₂-x), the content of the SnO₂ particles on SnS₂ surface can be simply regulated.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SnS2 shows hexagonal SnS2 (PDF#23-0677) and fcc Pt (PDF#04-0802). Pt-SnS2/SnO2-x shows tetragonal SnO2 (PDF#41-1445) peaks with diffraction peaks at 39.7° (Pt 111), 32.1° (SnS2 101), 26.6° (SnO2 110).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structures of various samples are characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Figure 2a; Figure S1, Supporting Information). Hexagonal phase SnS2 (PDF#23-0677) and fcc structure Pt (PDF#04-0802) peaks can be observed in the XRD pattern of Pt-SnS2. After oxidation, the characteristic peaks associated with tetragonal SnO2 (PDF#41-1445) appear in the patterns of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-x.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 shows SnS2 hexagonal structure maintained with SnO2 NPs covering surface and edges. Pt NPs uniformly dispersed with average diameter 4.5±0.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image of Pt-SnS2/SnO2 90 (Figure 2b) indicates that after the partial oxidation, the hexagonal structure of SnS2 is well maintained and covered by the newly formed SnO2 NPs. ... After Pt loading, Pt NPs are uniformly dispersed on the SnS2/SnO2 support with an average diameter of 4.5±0.3 nm and a narrow size distribution.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 shows heterostructures with lattice fringes 0.269 nm (SnS2 101), 0.336 nm (SnO2 110), 0.226 nm (Pt 111). Pt NPs mainly anchored at SnS2/SnO2 interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image of Pt-SnS2/SnO2 90 (Figure 2c) reveals the heterostructures formed by SnS2 layer and SnO2 particles, and Pt NPs are mainly anchored at the interfaces of SnS2 and SnO2. The lattice fringes are measured to be 0.269, 0.336, and 0.226 nm, corresponding to inter-plane spacings of the SnS2 (101), SnO2 (110), and Pt (111) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 shows Pt NPs preferentially loaded at SnS2/SnO2 heterointerfaces and interact more closely with SnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX mapping images (Figure 2d) also indicate that Pt NPs are inclined to load at the SnS2/SnO2 heterointerfaces and tend to interact more closely with SnO2, likely due to the stronger bond strength of Pt-O than Pt-S.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SnS2/SnO2 shows S 2p peaks at 162.78 eV (S-Sn) and 169.28 eV (S-O) with S-O/S-Sn ratio maximum 0.63/0.37 at 90 min. Pt 4f7/2 of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 at 71.45 eV shows negative shift vs Pt/C (71.80 eV), indicating electron transfer to Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For three Pt-SnS2/SnO2 samples, two distinct peaks at 162.78 and 169.28 eV can be ascribed to the S-Sn and S-O bonds. ... The binding energy of Pt0 4f7/2 peak in Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 (71.45 eV) shows a negative shift compared to that of commercial Pt/C (71.80 eV), indicating the electron transfer from SnS2/SnO2 to Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 shows reduced white line intensity vs Pt-SnS2 indicating electron transfer to Pt. EXAFS shows Pt-O and Pt-S peaks confirming interface loading, Pt-Pt bond length 2.753 Å (vs 2.765 Å foil).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The reduced white line intensity of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 demonstrates more electron transfer from SnS2/SnO2 support to Pt... Obviously, the peaks of Pt-O and Pt-S simultaneously appear in Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90... EXAFS results reveal that the Pt-Pt bond length of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 (2.753 Å) is slightly decreased compared to the Pt foil (2.765 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band XPS shows d-band center of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 at -3.78 eV (downshifted 0.19 eV vs Pt/C at -3.59 eV), Pt-SnS2 at -3.99 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the d-band center of Pt-SnS2/SnO2·90 (-3.78 eV) is located at a more suitable position than Pt/C and Pt-SnS2 (-3.99 eV), which should benefit the Pt-O binding during ORR.

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 is 48.3 m² gPt⁻¹ (Hupd) and 51.2 m² gPt⁻¹ (CO-stripping), significantly larger than Pt-SnS2 (19.3/20.4 m² gPt⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSAs of Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90, Pt-SnS2, and Pt/C... are 48.3, 19.3, and 50.6 m² gPt⁻¹ respectively... the ECSAs... by CO stripping voltammetry... are 51.2, 20.4, and 52.3 m² gPt⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS after ADT shows Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 white line intensity almost unchanged, indicating stable chemical state and electron density of Pt atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specially, the white line intensity of Pt-SnS2/SnO2 90 is almost unchanged after 50 000 potential cycles (Figure 3c), demonstrating that the chemical state and electron density of Pt atoms in Pt-SnS2/SnO2 90 is rather stable during ADT.

nodes.characterization_summary: After ADT, Pt-SnS2/SnO2-90 shows insignificant Pt NP agglomeration and intact SnS2/SnO2 heterostructures morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for Pt-SnS2/SnO2 90, the Pt NPs reveal insignificant agglomeration and the morphology of the SnS2/SnO2 heterostructures is still clearly visible and integral (Figure S7a-c, Supporting Information).
